The dataset is structurally sound (1200 rows, 24 cols, clean binary target with 69/31 class balance and no missing target values), but it is not ready to train as-is: it needs cleaning first.

Three numeric columns — num_feature_04, num_feature_08 and num_feature_12 — contain sentinel/impossible values at max = 9999 while their medians are only ~54-62. That inflates their means to ~127-131 with std of ~825-846 (roughly 65x the std of comparable features), so these are almost certainly placeholder codes for missing rather than real measurements. Left untreated they will dominate any distance- or gradient-based model.

Missingness is also material and monotone across the categorical block: num_feature_03 (6%), num_feature_04 (8.5%), num_feature_14 (8.6%) on the numeric side, growing through cat_feature_04 (12.7%), cat_feature_05 (13.9%), cat_feature_06 (19.5%) and cat_feature_07 (22.1%). cat_feature_07 alone is a fifth missing and has cardinality 31 (cf. cat_feature_05 at 23 and cat_feature_06 at 27), so imputation plus high-cardinality encoding is required — median/mode imputation with explicit missing indicators, or dropping very-high-missing / very-high-cardinality columns, is a reasonable path.

Outlier counts are otherwise modest (e.g. 8 z-score outliers in both num_feature_04 and num_feature_08, consistent with the sentinel contamination), and several numeric features (num_feature_05, num_feature_10) have zero missingness and look clean.

Recommended: treat 9999 as missing before imputing, decide explicitly on an imputation/encoding strategy for the 10-22% missing block, winsorize or rank-transform the heavy-tailed numerics, then re-profile. Scaling and class weighting for the 31% minority class are also worth considering.

The target is clean (0% missing) with a modest 69/31 class imbalance that needs only mild attention. Recommended checks: (1) confirm 9999 is a sentinel and not a legitimate reading by inspecting value freqs; (2) verify whether the missing rate in the cat_feature_0X chain is monotone by row, which would indicate a single cascade source; (3) decide sentinel handling (drop vs impute) before fitting; (4) verify signup_date range has no future/placeholder dates; (5) re-profile after cleaning.

The dataset has a clean, well-populated target (binary, 0=0.689 / 1=0.311) and 1200 rows, but it is not ready to train as-is for three reasons.

1) Sentinel/extreme values: num_feature_04, num_feature_08 and num_feature_12 each have max=9999.0 while their medians sit near 54-62, producing std of ~825-846 against a mean of ~127. These look like sentinel/missing-codes injected into otherwise tight distributions, not real measurements. They must be recoded as missing or capped, otherwise models will be dominated by these values.

2) Missingness: 4 columns exceed 10% missing (cat_feature_07 at 22.1%, cat_feature_06 at 19.5%, cat_feature_05 at 13.9%, cat_feature_04 at 12.7%), and several numeric columns are near 8.5% (num_feature_14 8.58%, num_feature_04 8.5%, num_feature_09 8.25%). Complete cases would drop a meaningful share of the 1200 rows, so an explicit imputation or missing-indicator strategy is needed; tree models can tolerate it, linear models cannot.

3) High-cardinality categoricals: cat_feature_07 (31 levels), cat_feature_06 (27), cat_feature_05 (23), cat_feature_04 (19) will explode under one-hot encoding, and each already has substantial missingness. These need grouping/rare-level collapsing or target/ordinal encoding.

Outlier counts are moderate and plausible for most numeric features (IQR counts 7-15; z-score counts 1-8) except for the three sentinel-contaminated columns. No zero-inflation issue (all zero_ratio 0.0), and is_active, signup_date and target carry no missing values.

Recommendation: treat as needs_cleaning - handle the 9999 sentinels, choose and document imputation, and decide on encoding for the high-cardinality categoricals before training. Verify the sentinel hypothesis with value-frequency counts and confirm the class balance after cleaning.

1) Sentinel values: num_feature_04, num_feature_08 and num_feature_12 all have max = 9999 against otherwise ~50-70 ranges (their q75 values are ~63, 67, 70) and stds of 846/828/825 versus ~12 for every other numeric column. This is a classic 9999 placeholder-code leak, not a real measurement, and will dominate any distance- or gradient-based model. These three columns should have the sentinel recoded to missing (or imputed) before training.

2) Missingness: missingness is pervasive, though no column exceeds 22%. Structurally the categorical block degrades monotonically (cat_feature_04 12.7% -> cat_feature_05 13.9% -> cat_feature_06 19.5% -> cat_feature_07 22.1%), with cardinality rising alongside (19, 23, 27, 31), which suggests these fields are only populated for a subset of records and the "missing" is likely informative. Numeric missingness tops out around 8.6% (num_feature_14). Every column needs an explicit imputation policy (and, for the categoricals, possibly an explicit "missing" level) rather than a default.

3) Outliers: IQR outliers appear in every numeric column at roughly 7-15 counts, which is mild, but for the three sentinel-contaminated columns the outlier counts are confounded with the 9999 codes and cannot be interpreted until that is fixed.

4) Target: target is a two-class label with moderate imbalance (~69% / 31%); accuracy alone will be misleading, so plan a stratified split and evaluate with PR-AUC / F1 as well.

Recommended next steps: recode 9999 sentinels to NaN and re-profile, choose and document imputation per column, verify whether categorical missingness is MCAR or informative, and use stratified evaluation. With those steps the dataset should be trainable.
